clue.text: Watering hole around international hotel in seaside resort

indicators.note: the watering hole is placed around the letter, so it wraps it

parts.note: a watering hole is a pub, a bar
the Ritz is the famous London hotel

explanation.surface: A drinker's bar near a grand international hotel in a fashionable coastal town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts BAR around I, giving BIAR; the Ritz then completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Biarritz is a fashionable town on the Basque coast of south-west France, famous for beaches and surfing.

clue.text: See 24
Climbing mountain, I'm surprised to create excitement

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an Alp is a mountain
ooh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A climber reaching the summit exclaims in thrilled surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns ALPOOH, mountain plus surprised cry, upside down in this down clue, so it reads HOOPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is noisy fuss and commotion, a burst of exuberant publicity or ballyhoo.

clue.text: Loners I help to entertain recently

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the distress call holds the other word

parts.note: SOS is the distress call, a cry for help
late can mean recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: Someone helping to look after people who keep to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertain' reads as hosting guests, which is exactly how the distress call holds the word for recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolates are people or things set apart from others, solitary individuals cut off from a group.

clue.text: Fancy lager and beer bottles right for bulky characters

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at an elaborate rearrangement of the drink's letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bottles here means holds inside, as a bottle holds its contents

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker likes lager and beer bottles, as a route to getting bulky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulky characters' sounds like stout people, but characters are printed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Large print is text set in a big typeface for readers with poor sight, so its letters are bulky.

clue.text: Part of blood line going through grandmother

indicators.note: the line passes through the middle of the relative, so it sits inside

parts.note: a grandmother can be your pa's ma, father's mother

explanation.surface: A family bloodline running down through a grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: Read grandmother as PA'S MA, your father's mother; 'going through' runs L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale yellow liquid component of blood in which the cells are suspended.

clue.text: Man serving extravagant old artist

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, a man serving in the army
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A waiter putting on an over-the-top show for an elderly painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man serving' looks like a waiter; it is a soldier, GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto di Bondone was the Florentine painter of the early Renaissance, known for the Arena Chapel frescoes.

clue.text: As much clothing used to be smart, husband's seen inside it

indicators.note: the husband appears within the combined letters, placed in the middle

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
able means clever, smart

explanation.surface: A husband appearing in clothes that were once smart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after husband stands for 'is'; 'seen inside' puts H between WAS and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Much clothing is capable of being laundered in water without damage, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: People called Barbara in swanky residence

parts.note: the people are two Barbaras; the first is the actress Barbara Windsor
the second person called Barbara is the Labour politician Barbara Castle

explanation.surface: A family of Barbaras living in some posh house.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Windsor was an EastEnders and Carry On actress; Barbara Castle was a Labour cabinet minister. Their surnames together name the royal home.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor Castle in Berkshire is a royal residence of the British monarch, about as grand as homes get.

clue.text: Teacher this person backed, one controlling a pupil

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher
this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: A teacher supported by the setter, keeping a pupil in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild beside the teacher, but it is the opening of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured ring of the eye whose muscles widen and narrow the pupil.

clue.text: Top sloe gin mixed for expert in the jug

indicators.note: mixed as in a cocktail, the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-rate sloe gin served up, perhaps in a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: The jug is slang for prison, not a drinks vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A penologist studies prisons and the punishment of criminals; jug is old slang for jail.

clue.text: Covering face, girl blunders on the phone

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the girl's title goes around the face

parts.note: miss is a young girl
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: A girl hides her face, embarrassed after blundering on a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a clock face, the dial, not a person's face.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdial is to make a mistake while entering a telephone number, reaching the wrong person.

clue.text: Youth attending parties, broadcasting covers of LadBaby with style

parts.note: a deb, a debutante, is a young woman attending society parties
on air means broadcasting

indicators.note: covers are the outside, so only the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of LadBaby

explanation.surface: A young partygoer playing cover versions of LadBaby songs on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: LadBaby is a British YouTuber with a run of Christmas number-one charity cover singles, so 'covers' is apt on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonairly means in a suave, charming and confident manner, so with style and polish.

clue.text: Game of Diplomacy about to incorporate a little cash

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so the other letters go inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
a is one, I
P, penny, is a small amount of cash

explanation.surface: Playing the board game Diplomacy for small stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomacy' looks like the name of the board game; it is TACT, which 'about' turns into TCAT. 'to incorporate' puts I (one) and P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is an old street game in which a tapered piece of wood is struck at one end to flip it up.

clue.text: Zombie's outside? Fetch guards over one's seen in street

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the possessive: the zombie's outside, its outer letters

indicators.note: guards means surrounds to protect, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: to fetch is to bring
across can mean over, as in to go over a road

explanation.surface: A zombie lurks outside; someone goes to fetch the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like people to fetch, but it is the containment signal; 'over' means across, as when going over a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra crossing is a pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes across a road.

clue.text: One examining Jenny? Also Oscar and Rex

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, playfully an ass-ess, a she-ass like lioness
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
R is the abbreviation of Rex, king

explanation.surface: Three names, Jenny, Oscar and Rex, as if sitting an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: female ass, made like lioness, gives ASSESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates and judges, for instance an examiner who marks work or values property for tax.

clue.text: Travel in minor thoroughfare south of Indian region

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so this piece comes after

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a B road is a minor road in Britain

explanation.surface: Journeying along a small road below a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are secondary roads below A roads in the numbering system.
explanation.definitionFit: To go abroad is to journey to a foreign country, which is a kind of travelling.

clue.text: Rolling Stones material is for a younger singer

indicators.note: rolling sends the letters tumbling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rolling Stones songs being suitable for a more youthful performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' looks part of the band's name but is the anagram signal for all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alanis Morissette is the Canadian rock vocalist of Jagged Little Pill, decades younger than the Stones.

clue.text: Dish in oven, initially halved

indicators.note: the first letter is cut in half as a Roman numeral, a hundred becoming fifty

parts.note: a cooker is an oven

explanation.surface: A dish cooking in the oven, cut in half to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter C is 100 in Roman numerals; halved it is 50, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal for an attractive person, and a looker is someone very good-looking.

clue.text: Dated cooler Spanish tennis player over time

indicators.note: over means covering, so the tennis player's name sits over the letter and holds it

parts.note: Carlos Alcaraz is the Spanish tennis champion

explanation.surface: A Spanish tennis star cooling down after going over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooler is slang for prison, and dated because the island jail closed in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz is the former island prison in San Francisco Bay, shut since 1963, so a jail of the past.

clue.text: Python shelters in church

indicators.note: the shelters are placed in the church, inside its letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
lees are sheltered places, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A snake taking refuge inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Python looks like the snake; it is a member of Monty Python.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cleese was a founder member of the Monty Python comedy team.

clue.text: See 17
Writer's life filled with reading, say

indicators.note: the life story is filled with the letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story
reading is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: An author's life spent reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' flags that reading is an example of an R, one of the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, a thing to write with, named after its inventor László Bíró.

clue.text: Money in Madison County, but not all of it

indicators.note: not all of it means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Money in Madison County, though not the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes The Bridges of Madison County, but County is Bucks, Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is American slang for a dollar, the money used in Madison, Wisconsin.

clue.text: A steak may be so good for you

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an exclamation of praise

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase is a cooking degree for meat, the other a congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak can be cooked thoroughly, and the phrase is also said to congratulate someone on an achievement.

clue.text: One feeding wild cats sushi which could be better

indicators.note: feeding means going into, as food goes in, so the letter goes inside
wild signals the letters running loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone feeding sushi to feral cats, not an ideal diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges CATS SUSHI; 'feeding' puts I in among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of something mediocre: the phrase concedes that it is poor or inadequate, for what it's worth.
